reason: Wording checked. Peden renders the Respuesta passage "... I often say, when observing these trivial details: had Aristotle prepared victuals, he would have written more." (Poems, Protest, and a Dream, Penguin 1997, p. 43, as cited with page by Metanexus; the LARB essay prints the same sentence). Trimming to the clause after the colon and capitalising its first word mints nothing. Attribution right (the Respuesta, 1691, printed 1700, is a letter to the bishop of Puebla writing as Sor Filotea, so Correspondence is the right tag). shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, not at cap, not banned. Source line 128 chars, leads with the name, colon-free and dash-free. In scope and publishable. Only weakness: the 1982 Lime Rock edition was not opened by anyone; the wording is confirmed in the 1997 Penguin reprint of the same translation, so the citation should name that.
betterCitation: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, Reply to Sor Filotea de la Cruz, the philosophies of the kitchen (trans. Margaret Sayers Peden, Penguin, 1997, p. 43)
